name: Twisted Electrons TWISTfm
description: Twisted Electrons TWISTfm FM synthesizer: its performance and fader controllers, and every parameter of its SysEx editor protocol, read back with GET_ALL.

sources.title: TWISTfm manual (web page)
sources.notes: The page's MIDI tables (Direct Performance CCs, Main Fader CCs, SysEx Editor Protocol, SysEx Responses, Editor SysEx Parameter Index), read by tools/profiles/twisted/read-twisted-page.mjs from te-manual-twistfm.html saved 2026-11-11 (sha256 d4e81752c767969aa91f2919aa66f8efa83a5a797d676b05e089e0bd64c2137a), https://www.twisted-electrons.com/pages/manual-twistfm. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/twisted/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/twisted/synths/, not this file.
Every controller is a row of the page's Direct Performance CCs and Main Fader CCs, sent as the controller it prints on the channel variable. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.
The page is a live document, saved on 2026-11-11; a later version may differ.

The editor parameters are the SysEx Editor Protocol's (header F0 7D 54 57 30): SET editor parameter (03) with the parameter's id and its value in two 7-bit bytes, the low first ("value = LSB + (MSB * 128)"). Pull sends GET_ALL editor parameters (F0 7D 54 57 30 01 F7) and reads its answer, an INFO message (11) and a VALUE message (12 id valueLSB valueMSB) for each of the 113 editor IDs: each parameter takes the value of the VALUE whose id is its own, so the order they come in does not matter. The collection is complete at 114 messages.

Left out, controllers whose printed values go past 127, which a controller cannot carry: CC 7 Master vol (0-255); CC 101 BPM (1-500); CC 104 Morph pos (0-255); CC 114 Seq length (1-128) (the editor parameters and raw preset addresses carry the full values).
Not laid out: the raw preset and raw setting addresses (commands 05 - 0A), which carry the same settings as the controllers and the editor parameters byte by byte, and the buffer commands (0C, 0D).
